metadata_filter_field.name: chapter
metadata_filter_field.value_source: Chapter number shown in the source PDF headings and page headers.

questions.question: How do judges use precedent when deciding a case under the common-law system?
questions.expected_answer: They consult previous rulings in similar cases to inform their decision.
questions.evidence_quote: judges rely on precedent, i.e., previous court rulings on similar cases, when determining the ruling in their own cases.

questions.question: In chapter 2, why might disputing parties prefer mediation when they want to keep a sensitive dispute private?
questions.expected_answer: Mediation can preserve anonymity because court proceedings become public record.
questions.evidence_quote: Since court proceedings become a matter of public record, it can be advantageous to use mediation to preserve anonymity.

questions.question: What does the text mean by dyadic negotiation?
questions.expected_answer: Two individuals interact to try to resolve a dispute.
questions.evidence_quote: Put simply, dyadic negotiation involves two individuals interacting with one another in an attempt to resolve a dispute.

questions.question: What makes arbitration involuntary rather than voluntary?
questions.expected_answer: An outside party requires the disputants to attempt arbitration before litigation.
questions.evidence_quote: this requirement is known as involuntary arbitration because it is forced upon them by an outside party.

questions.question: In chapter 4, when can a state's use of police power affecting interstate commerce be unconstitutional?
questions.expected_answer: When it interferes with or discriminates against interstate commerce.
questions.evidence_quote: If the exercise of the power interferes with, or discriminates against, interstate commerce, then the action is generally deemed to be unconstitutional.

questions.question: How does the arbitrator decide a baseball arbitration award?
questions.expected_answer: The arbitrator selects one party's offer without modifying it.
questions.evidence_quote: the arbitrator chooses one offer or the other, without modification.

questions.question: Name two organizational benefits the text associates with ethical business practices.
questions.expected_answer: Examples include improved recruitment and retention, better customer relationships, and positive public relations.
questions.evidence_quote: Ethical business practices, guided by a corporate set of standards, can have many positive outcomes, including recruitment and retention improvement, better relationships with customers, and positive PR.

questions.question: How does money laundering make proceeds from crime appear legitimate?
questions.expected_answer: It passes the proceeds through otherwise legitimate businesses so they appear clean and cannot be tied back to the illegal acts.
questions.evidence_quote: passing it through otherwise legitimate businesses so that it appears

questions.question: What action does the text identify as larceny in a business setting?
questions.expected_answer: Unlawfully taking another person's or a business's personal property.
questions.evidence_quote: Larceny occurs when a person unlawfully takes the personal property of another person or a business.

questions.question: In chapter 7, what are offer and acceptance in forming a contract?
questions.expected_answer: An offer proposes entering a contract; acceptance agrees to be bound by its terms.
questions.evidence_quote: An offer is a proposal made to demonstrate an intent to enter a contract. Acceptance is the agreement to be bound by the terms of the offer.

questions.question: Can a minor void a contract for necessities such as food or clothing?
questions.expected_answer: In most states, a contract for necessities may not be voided by the minor.
questions.evidence_quote: In most states, a contract for necessities (i.e. food and clothing) may not be voided.

questions.question: Under the UCC, when does a merchant supplier retain the risk of loss for goods?
questions.expected_answer: Until the buyer takes possession of the goods.
questions.evidence_quote: as long as the supplier is considered a merchant, the risk of loss remains with the merchant until the buyer takes possession of the good.

questions.question: What happens after a workers' compensation agency determines that an injury claim is legitimate?
questions.expected_answer: Compensation benefits are paid.
questions.evidence_quote: If the injury is determined to be legitimate, compensation benefits are paid accordingly.

questions.question: How does the text define administrative law?
questions.expected_answer: It is delegated power granted to administrative agencies to carry out specific functions.
questions.evidence_quote: Administrative law is basically the delegated power granted to administrative agencies to carry out specific functions.

questions.question: What market concern led lawmakers to address large-company mergers and similar practices in the late 1800s?
questions.expected_answer: The risk that large companies would create monopolies or control markets.
questions.evidence_quote: attempts by large companies to create monopolies or to control the market, led state and federal lawmakers to take steps to reduce the risks associated with this type of practice.

questions.question: In chapter 12, what must a plaintiff show to establish an unfair trade practice without proving intent?
questions.expected_answer: The practice itself must be shown to be unfair or deceptive; intent need not be proved.
questions.evidence_quote: Plaintiffs do not have to prove intent. Showing that the practice itself was unfair or deceptive is sufficient.

questions.question: Which three sources of shared principles does the text identify as relevant to enforcing international law?
questions.expected_answer: Customs, treaties, and organizations.
questions.evidence_quote: the principles set forth by globally shared customs, treaties, and organizations.

questions.question: In chapter 14, what is the purpose of the Securities Exchange Act's reporting requirements for public companies?
questions.expected_answer: To keep the public informed of changes that could affect securities prices.
questions.evidence_quote: The purpose of these requirements was transparency, that is, keeping the public up to date and informed of changes that might impact securities prices.

questions.question: What are state securities laws intended to combat fraud commonly called?
questions.expected_answer: Blue sky laws.
questions.evidence_quote: state-level securities laws aimed to combat fraud are called blue sky laws.

questions.question: Why can group negotiation be more difficult to resolve than a two-person negotiation?
questions.expected_answer: It involves more than two parties and is often more complex, time-consuming, and challenging to resolve.
questions.evidence_quote: Group negotiation involves more than two individuals or parties, and by its very nature, it is often more complex, time-consuming, and challenging to resolve.
